source.title: Predicting pragmatic reasoning in language games

confidence_rationale: The founding Rational Speech Act result: a model in which speakers choose utterances to be informative to a Bayesian listener -- i.e. to maximise the listener's probability of recovering the intended referent, equivalently to reduce the listener's uncertainty -- gives a close, parameter-free fit to human judgments in referential games. This is ARC-117's selection objective stated formally and fitted to data. Discounted because the games are tiny, one-shot and referential, and the fit is to judgments about speakers rather than to an adversarial test against a sender-salience model.
failure_signatures: The model's fit is to simple reference games with a handful of objects and features; it does not show receiver-objective selection outperforming sender-salience selection under a bound channel in a coordination task, which is ARC-117's falsifier.

A salience-based speaker prior is not ruled out: the paper's informativeness term and a salience prior make overlapping predictions in scenes where the most distinctive feature is also the most salient.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Behaviour in simple referential communication games is modelled by assuming speakers attempt to be informative and listeners use Bayesian inference to recover the intended referent; the model gives a close, parameter-free fit to human judgments.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-117 asks that utterance selection approximate a sufficient statistic for the receiver: say what most reduces their uncertainty about your state. RSA's speaker, who picks the word that maximises the listener's posterior on the intended referent, is that objective in its simplest form. It predicts WHAT gets said, not merely that something is said, which is the specificity ARC-117 claims.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Referent identification in a closed set is a much narrower 'sender state' than the affective and intentional states REE senders would communicate. The listener model here is hand-specified, not learned; REE would need the receiver model itself to be learned, which is the substrate ARC-117 notes does not exist.
mapping.source_context: Adult participants (online) in one-shot referential games with small sets of objects varying on simple features; speaker and listener judgments compared to a Bayesian model.

confidence_components.notes: Science brief; the RSA framework it launched has a large confirming literature. Mapping good on the objective, weaker on the task and the falsifier's comparison arm.
